answer: Diminishing-returns stake weighting resists sybils: influence is a concave function of locked stake, so early collateral buys much weight and each extra unit buys less, nearing a zenith it never reaches. This REQUIRES identity binding — else splitting stake across a dune of accounts each sits on the steep low end and dodges the concavity, so it only works one-curve-per-identity. Bound that way, a swarm's fragmented stake earns strictly LESS total weight than one consolidated honest holder — the echo of diminishing returns makes fragmentation pointless.
